# Implementation Plan: Codex member native spawn subagents (D-002, dual v1+v2)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-member-skill-agent-subagent-fanout"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-09. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

## Overview

When a Ralph crew member runs on the **codex** engine, the write/review
subagent sites it needs for a full `/implement-with-ralph` are currently broken
in two ways: (1) the two highest-value sites — **Phase 2 PRD generation** and
the **Phase 5a/5b code/docs reviewers** — are described in the shared skill
source as free-form prose ("Spawn an Agent subagent ...") with no literal
`Agent(` token, so the codex generator's scanner never lowers them and a codex
member executes them **inline in its own context** (hand-scaffolded `prd.json`,
in-context self-review); and (2) the sites that *are* lowered emit a
**schema-stale, v2-only** recipe (`spawn_agent { task_name, fork_turns }` +
`followup_task`, omitting the v2-required `message`, and STOPping outright on a
default-config v1 member).

This plan makes every clean-context write/review subagent a **native codex
`spawn_agent` child** (operator override **D-002**, codex-purity — NOT the
brainstorm's D-001 copilot-exec hybrid), supporting **BOTH** codex v1 (Collab)
and v2 (MultiAgentV2) via a runtime detect-and-branch recipe. The native
write-child primitive is already proven GO for both surfaces (two live smokes,
`69de6def` v2 / `9beb869a` v1) — feasibility is closed; this is a generator/
lowering change only.

The change is **plugin-side, codex-only**: it touches the codex lowering layer,
the generator wiring, tests, generated `.codex-plugin/` artifacts, and release
metadata. It does **not** touch the `codex/` submodule, and (per the chosen
design) it does **not** change the shared `skills/*/SKILL.md` prose, so the
Claude source and the Copilot generated/hand-fork artifacts remain byte-identical
(zero cross-engine parity churn). The ship gate is a live codex-member
`/implement-with-ralph` dogfood proving real delegation with git + transcript
evidence — the precondition for re-enabling `CREWS_ENGINE=codex` as default.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
All paths are relative to the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule. Ralph is at
**5.55.0**. The codex lowering layer `scripts/codex-lowering.mjs` is a **markdown
rewriter**: it rewrites delegation sites in source `SKILL.md` into multi-agent
**recipe PROSE** that a codex member reads and self-executes at runtime — there
is no JS that calls `spawn_agent`; emitting "native spawn" means emitting correct
recipe prose.

### Technical Constraints
- **Detect by tool presence, not config probe** (v2 wins if both features on;
  exactly one surface is ever active): `list_agents`/`followup_task` present ⇒
  v2; namespaced `multi_agent_v1.*` + `send_input`/`resume_agent` and NO
  `list_agents` ⇒ v1; neither ⇒ the only legitimate STOP.
- **Per-system recipe (tool sets, schemas, retrieval all differ).** Each recipe
  is a complete, EXECUTABLE tool sequence — every step names its required args so
  the generated recipe is not merely conceptual (F-004):
  - **v2** (plain tool names): `spawn_agent{task_name, message}` →
    `wait_agent{timeout_ms}` → `list_agents` → `agents[].agent_status.completed` →
    `JSON.parse` → `close_agent{target: <agent_name-or-id>}`. (`spawn_agent`
    requires `message` under `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`; `close_agent`
    requires a `target`.)
  - **v1** (NAMESPACED tool names — `multi_agent_v1.spawn_agent`,
    `multi_agent_v1.wait_agent`, `multi_agent_v1.close_agent`) (F-005): the FULL
    task goes in `multi_agent_v1.spawn_agent{message}` as a **one-shot**
    delegation — `send_input`/`resume_agent` are NOT used by the recipe (no
    follow-up dispatch step) (F-003) → `multi_agent_v1.wait_agent{targets:[agent_id],
    timeout_ms}` → read `status[agent_id].completed` → `JSON.parse` →
    `multi_agent_v1.close_agent{target: <agent_id>}`. (No `followup_task`/
    `list_agents` — they do not exist on v1; do not rely on `task_name`.)
  - Shared: `fork_turns:"none"` analog (v1 default `fork_context:false`; do not
    set `fork_context:true`); omit `agent_type`/`model`/`reasoning_effort`;
    `timeout_ms >= 10000`; single-level fan-out only; FAIL HARD on `timed_out`
    or malformed JSON.
- **Shared working tree**: spawn children share the parent's tree (no per-child
  sandbox) ⇒ writes parent-visible immediately; concurrent write-children need
  DISJOINT WRITE SETS. The fixer/updater/reviewer sites are sequential (safe);
  the Phase-5.5 fan-out trio is read-only retrospectives (safe).
- **`CODEX_FORBIDDEN`** must stay clean (no `Agent(`/`Skill(`/`task(` in codex
  output). Under the chosen design the shared prose is unchanged (it contains
  bare "Agent", never `Agent(`), so FORBIDDEN is not at risk from the prose.
- Plugin-side only; **no `codex/` submodule edit**. `features.multi_agent_v2`
  enablement is coordination-only (`codex-engine-ralph-member-enablement`) — the
  dual-support means a default-config (v1) member already works without it.

## Approach

### Architecture

**Key design decision — how to lower the two PROSE-ONLY sites.** Two options
were evaluated; both independent research lenses (architect + Copilot xhigh)
converged on **(B)**.

- **(A) Convert prose → literal `Agent(` in shared source.** Reuses the existing
  scanner/inventory/drift-guard verbatim and is consistent with the 8 already-
  lowered literal sites. BUT: it changes the shared `skills/*/SKILL.md` for ALL
  engines, forcing a Copilot regen AND an `implement-with-ralph` Copilot
  **hand-fork** edit-in-lockstep (parity-exceptions), and the review-changes
  reviewer is **scope-conditioned** (code vs docs vs disabled-security) which a
  single literal `Agent(` cannot express cleanly.
- **(B) CHOSEN — codex-only prose-site lowering keyed by stable anchors.** Add an
  **exported** `PROSE_SITE_INVENTORY` (stable `siteId` + a **block-capture rule**:
  a `startAnchor` substring AND an `endAnchor` substring (or an explicit
  line/heading boundary) that together delimit the WHOLE prose block to replace —
  a single anchor is NOT enough because both sites are multi-line blocks
  (PRD-gen = line 277 + its follow-on bullets 278-280; reviewer = the scope table
  117-121 + the spawn sentence 123), so anchoring on just "Spawn an Agent
  subagent…" would strip one sentence and leave stale surrounding instructions —
  F-007/F-010) + subagent type(s) + scope-conditionality + the child prompt) and a
  capture/replace pass in `codex-lowering.mjs` that swaps the FULL delimited block
  for the native-spawn recipe, plus a `verifyProseSiteInventory` drift guard that
  FAILS the build if a `startAnchor`/`endAnchor` is missing, duplicated, or
  out-of-order (same protection the literal-`Agent` inventory gives). The
  inventory + guard are exported and directly unit-tested, mirroring
  `AGENT_SITE_INVENTORY`/`verifyAgentSiteInventory` (F-008). **Decisive advantage:** the shared source prose is UNCHANGED,
  so Claude source + Copilot generated/hand-fork artifacts stay byte-identical —
  zero cross-engine parity churn; ONLY `.codex-plugin/` changes. The stable-anchor
  guard neutralizes (B)'s only real objection (prose-edit brittleness): an anchor
  that drifts fails CI loudly rather than silently dropping the lowering.

Both the new prose sites and the existing literal-`Agent(` sites share **one
recipe builder** that emits the dual v1/v2 detect-and-branch + per-system
recipe, so fixing the builder fixes the schema-stale bug everywhere at once.

### Implementation Strategy
Ordered so the foundation (recipe builder) lands before the consumers, tests
before regen, and the dogfood last as the ship gate:

1. **Recipe builder + message-fix + dual-branch** in `codex-lowering.mjs`:
   refactor `singleDelegationRecipe`/`fanOutRecipe` (or extract a shared
   `nativeSpawnRecipe(payload, shape)`) to emit the detect-and-branch preamble
   (replacing the v2-required `preflightProse` STOP) and per-system v1/v2 recipe
   bodies; v2 carries the task in `spawn_agent.message` and drops `followup_task`
   as the task carrier; v1 uses `spawn_agent{message}` →
   `wait_agent{targets,timeout_ms}` → `status[target].completed`. This fixes ALL
   8 existing literal sites simultaneously. STOP only when neither surface exists.
2. **Prose-site mechanism** in `codex-lowering.mjs`: an **exported**
   `PROSE_SITE_INVENTORY` (each entry: `siteId` + `startAnchor`/`endAnchor` block
   bounds + subagent type(s) + scope-conditionality + child prompt) +
   `captureProseSites`/`lowerProseSites` (run inside `applyCodexSubstitutions`
   BEFORE the FORBIDDEN check, reusing the recipe builder, replacing the WHOLE
   delimited block) + an exported `verifyProseSiteInventory` drift guard.
3. **Register the two sites** in `PROSE_SITE_INVENTORY`: (a) implement-with-ralph
   Phase 2 PRD-gen (block 277-280; child prompt = read+follow `create-prd` then
   `convert-to-ralph-prd` with the autonomous flags / `--job` / engines /
   `--target-repo` inputs); (b) review-changes Step 2 reviewer (block 113-129;
   the emitted recipe is **scope-conditioned**: scope=code → `code-reviewer`,
   scope=docs → `docs-reviewer`, and scope=security → an explicit inert/skip
   branch — Phase 5c is disabled so the recipe must NOT emit a live
   `security-reviewer` spawn, but it must preserve the security scope as a
   no-op/reject branch rather than silently dropping it (F-001/F-008)).
4. **Wire the guard** into `generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs` (call
   `verifyProseSiteInventory` alongside `verifyAgentSiteInventory` at ~295).
5. **Tests** in `tests/test-codex-generator.mjs`: dual v1/v2 recipe assertions;
   `message` present in every recipe; v2 no longer carries the task via
   `followup_task`; v1 recipe uses the namespaced `multi_agent_v1.*` tool names
   and never mentions `list_agents`/`followup_task`; `close_agent` always names a
   `target`; prose-site lowering replaces the WHOLE "Spawn an Agent subagent"
   block in generated codex artifacts (not just one sentence); prose-site drift
   guard fails on a missing/duplicated/out-of-order anchor; direct export +
   shape assertions on `PROSE_SITE_INVENTORY` (mirroring the `AGENT_SITE_INVENTORY`
   tests); the security-scope branch stays inert; `CODEX_FORBIDDEN` still clean;
   generated artifacts contain the recipe markers for the new sites. **Also update
   `tests/test-codex-live-smoke.mjs` (131-143)** — its current assertion pins the
   `spawn_agent → followup_task → wait_agent → list_agents → close_agent` shape,
   which the dual-branch breaks; change it to accept the detect-and-branch
   preamble + per-system sequences. Update the two pinning tests in
   test-codex-generator.mjs (US-003 preflight 227-251, US-005 sequence 395-452).
6. **Acceptance dogfood (US-006) — runs BEFORE the release-metadata bump.** A
   dogfood-forced recipe change must not ship behind stale version claims (F-009),
   so the live codex-member `/implement-with-ralph` proof (see US-006 below) runs
   and goes green first.
7. **Regenerate + gate + release**: `generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --target=codex
   --write`; assert ZERO diff in Copilot/Claude artifacts (only `.codex-plugin/`
   changes); run the Codex Release Gate; bump ralph version across the six stamps
   + three marketplace indexes; add CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md behavioral note. This is
   the LAST step, after the dogfood passes.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Native codex `spawn_agent` recipe for the write/review subagent sites, dual
  v1 (Collab) + v2 (MultiAgentV2), detect-and-branch by tool presence.
- Lower the two prose-only sites (PRD-gen, code/docs reviewers) via the codex-
  only prose-site mechanism + drift guard.
- Fix the schema-stale v2 emission (pass `message`, drop `followup_task` as the
  task carrier) across all lowered sites.
- Update generator wiring + tests + the Codex Release Gate; regenerate
  `.codex-plugin/` artifacts; bump version (six stamps + three indexes).
- The re-enable dogfood with git + transcript evidence.

### Out of Scope
- D-001 copilot-exec hybrid (rejected by operator override).
- Any `codex/` submodule change.
- Re-running the Phase 0 v1/v2 write-child smokes (already GO).
- Re-architecting the already-shipped read-only LENS fan-out (it inherits the
  message-fix + dual-branch via the shared builder but is not redesigned).
- `features.multi_agent_v2` enablement plumbing (coordination item; dual-support
  covers default v1) and re-enabling Phase 5c security (inert backplane only).

## Risk Areas
- **Prose-anchor drift (highest risk).** If a future edit to the shared skill
  prose changes the delimited block, the lowering silently stops or replaces the
  wrong span. Mitigated by `verifyProseSiteInventory` failing the build on a
  missing/duplicated/out-of-order `startAnchor`/`endAnchor` — the same drift
  protection the literal-`Agent` inventory provides. Anchors must be stable, unique
  substrings, and the inventory must capture the WHOLE block (start+end bounds) so
  no stale surrounding instruction survives the replacement.
- **Scope-conditionality of the reviewer site.** review-changes Step 2 picks the
  agent by `--scope`; the emitted recipe must branch (code→code-reviewer,
  docs→docs-reviewer) without leaking a `security-reviewer` recipe (Phase 5c
  disabled). Risk of an over-broad single recipe; mitigate with scope-keyed recipe
  text + a test asserting only code/docs recipes are emitted.
- **Recipe length / readability.** Dual v1/v2 doubles the recipe prose per site;
  generated artifacts grow. Acceptable (generated), but keep the shared preamble
  DRY so the per-site delta is small.
- **`FORBIDDEN` interaction.** The prose-site lowering must run BEFORE
  `assertNoCodexForbidden`; if it ran after, an un-lowered site's bare prose is
  fine (no `Agent(`) but a mis-registered anchor could leave the prose un-lowered
  and the member would self-execute. A test asserting the generated artifact no
  longer contains the anchor prose catches this.
- **Dogfood flakiness.** codex-exec has shown empty-output/hang behavior on this
  box (observed during Phase 2 research). The dogfood must capture the transcript
  to a file and assert on git state, not rely on streamed output.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. For a codex-generated `implement-with-ralph` / `review-changes` /
   `convert-to-ralph-prd`, the **PRD-gen, code-reviewer, and docs-reviewer** sites
   emit a native `spawn_agent` recipe (NOT inline self-execution, NOT a copilot-
   exec shell-out); the generated codex artifacts no longer contain the prose-only
   "Spawn an Agent subagent" block at those sites — the WHOLE delimited block
   (instruction sentence + surrounding bullets/table) is replaced by the recipe,
   leaving no stale fragments.
2. Every lowered write/review recipe emits a detect-and-branch preamble with BOTH
   a v1 and a v2 variant selected by tool presence, and STOPs only when NEITHER
   surface exists. The v2 variant passes the task in `spawn_agent.message` (no
   `followup_task` as the task carrier) and ends with `close_agent{target}`; the
   v1 variant uses the namespaced `multi_agent_v1.*` tools (`spawn_agent{message}`
   one-shot → `wait_agent{targets, timeout_ms}` → `status[agent_id].completed` →
   `close_agent{target}`) and never mentions `list_agents`/`followup_task`/
   `send_input`.
3. `PROSE_SITE_INVENTORY` covers the two new sites; `verifyProseSiteInventory`
   FAILS the build when a registered anchor is missing or duplicated (verified by
   a negative test).
4. `node plugins/ralph/scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs --target=codex
   --check`, `node plugins/ralph/tests/test-codex-generator.mjs`, and `node
   tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.mjs` all exit 0; `CODEX_FORBIDDEN`
   passes (no `Skill(`/`Agent(`/`task(` leak in codex output).
5. Regenerating with `--target=all --write` produces ZERO diff in
   `.copilot-plugin/**` and `.claude-plugin/**` skill artifacts (parity preserved);
   only `.codex-plugin/**` changes. `check-copilot-parity.mjs` passes.
6. Ralph version is bumped with all six stamps + three marketplace indexes in
   sync; CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md behavioral note added.
7. **Dogfood (concrete, reproducible).** A live codex crew member runs a full
   `/implement-with-ralph --autonomous` on a defined minimal fixture (a tiny
   throwaway repo/feature with ≥1 trivial story — e.g. "add a constant + a test"),
   exercised at least once on the **v2** surface
   (`features.multi_agent_v2=true`) and, ideally, once on the default **v1**
   surface; at minimum ONE full green run with evidence is required. Required
   produced artifacts: `<job_dir>/prd.json`, `<job_dir>/code-review-findings.json`,
   `<job_dir>/docs-review-findings.json`, ≥1 `feat:` git commit, and a captured
   codex transcript at a known path (e.g.
   `.ralph/jobs/<job>/codex-dogfood-transcript.jsonl`). Pass/fail assertions:
   (a) the transcript shows a `spawn_agent` (or `multi_agent_v1.spawn_agent`)
   tool call whose child performs the PRD-gen (`create-prd` + `convert-to-ralph-prd`)
   — `prd.json` is written by a spawn-child, NOT by the top-level member inline;
   (b) the transcript shows `spawn_agent` calls for the Phase-5a `code-reviewer`
   and Phase-5b `docs-reviewer` (and the `code-fixer`/`docs-updater` when findings
   exist), recovered via `wait_agent`→(`list_agents` on v2 / `status[target]` on
   v1); (c) NO evidence of the member hand-writing `prd.json` or finalizing review
   in its own context. The check is scripted (grep the transcript for the spawn
   tool-call markers + child task names; assert artifact existence + git log). This
   is the `CREWS_ENGINE=codex` re-enable gate; release metadata (AC6) is bumped
   only after this passes.
8. Typecheck/lint/tests for the ralph plugin pass (`node plugins/ralph/tests/run.mjs`
   for the codex generator suite at minimum).

- **US-001** — Dual v1/v2 native-spawn recipe builder + `message` schema-fix +
  detect-and-branch preamble (replaces the v2-required STOP) in `codex-lowering.mjs`.
  Fixes all 8 existing literal-`Agent(` sites at once.
- **US-002** — Prose-site lowering mechanism: `PROSE_SITE_INVENTORY` +
  `captureProseSites`/`lowerProseSites` (in `applyCodexSubstitutions`, pre-FORBIDDEN)
  + `verifyProseSiteInventory` drift guard; wire the guard into the generator.
- **US-003** — Register the two prose sites (Phase-2 PRD-gen; review-changes Step 2
  scope-conditioned code-reviewer/docs-reviewer) with stable anchors + child prompts.
- **US-004** — Tests: dual v1/v2 + `message` + namespaced-v1 + `close_agent{target}`
  + v1-no-`list_agents` + prose-site whole-block lowering + drift-guard +
  exported-`PROSE_SITE_INVENTORY` shape + security-scope-inert + FORBIDDEN +
  generated-marker assertions; update the pinning tests (test-codex-generator
  US-003 preflight 227-251, US-005 sequence 395-452) AND
  `test-codex-live-smoke.mjs` (131-143) recipe-shape assertion.
- **US-005** — Acceptance dogfood (runs BEFORE the release bump): live codex-member
  full `/implement-with-ralph` on the minimal fixture, v2 (and ideally v1) surface,
  with the scripted git + transcript evidence from AC7 (no hand-scaffolded prd.json,
  no in-context self-review). `CREWS_ENGINE=codex` re-enable gate.
- **US-006** — Regenerate `.codex-plugin/`; assert zero Copilot/Claude diff; run the
  Codex Release Gate; version bump (six stamps + three indexes) + CHANGELOG +
  AGENTS.md behavioral note. Runs LAST, only after US-005 is green, so a
  dogfood-forced recipe change does not ship behind stale version claims.

## Suggested Decomposition

All stories edit `codex-lowering.mjs` / its tests / the generated artifacts in a
tight dependency chain (US-001 → US-002 → US-003 → US-004 → US-005 → US-006), so
they share the same files and **must run serially** in one cluster. Parallelizing
would produce conflicting writes to `codex-lowering.mjs` and the generated
`.codex-plugin/` tree.

### Cluster: codex-native-spawn-dual-v1v2
- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=`plugins/ralph/scripts/codex-lowering.mjs`,
  `plugins/ralph/scripts/generate-copilot-artifacts.mjs`,
  `plugins/ralph/tests/test-codex-generator.mjs`,
  `plugins/ralph/.codex-plugin/**`, the six version stamps; exclusive=none;
  risk=high (single hot file + generated tree + release metadata).
- `execution_mode` rationale: Every story mutates the same lowering module, its
  tests, or the generated/versioned outputs derived from it, so they must be
  serialized; there is no disjoint file footprint to exploit for parallelism.

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <plan_job_dir>/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition <plan_job_dir>/suggested-decomposition.json`

## Open Questions
- **Recipe builder shape (impl-time choice).** Extract a shared
  `nativeSpawnRecipe(payload, shape, system)` vs. inline the dual-branch into the
  existing `singleDelegationRecipe`/`fanOutRecipe`. Recommendation: extract, to
  keep the v1/v2 branch DRY across single + fan-out; the impl story confirms.
- **Anchor granularity for the reviewer site.** Whether to register one prose
  site for review-changes Step 2 emitting a scope-conditioned recipe, or two
  sites (one per scope). Recommendation: one site, scope-conditioned recipe text,
  since the source prose is a single block (123) selecting by `--scope`.
- **Dogfood fixture (RESOLVED — see AC7/US-005).** The fixture, required
  artifacts, both v1+v2 modes, transcript path, and grep assertions are now
  specified in Acceptance Criterion 7. The remaining latitude is the exact
  trivial feature used (impl-time choice); the gate requires one full green run
  with evidence and ideally exercises both surfaces.
- The codex research lens returned empty during planning (codex-exec emitted 0
  bytes); the plan's source claims were grounded by the researcher + architect
  Explore agents + the Copilot xhigh lens instead.
